questions.q: What was the one thing Black Beauty missed in his new place?
choices: Liberty, or freedom to run as he liked
His mother's milk and her kind advice
Plenty of good oats and sweet hay
A clean, bright stable with a window

questions.q: For how long had Black Beauty had all the liberty he could wish for?
choices: Three years and a half
Ten years and more
About six months
Only a week or two
questions.evidence: For three years and a half of my life

questions.q: How did Black Beauty sometimes act when John took him out after he had had little exercise?
choices: He could not keep quiet and wanted to jump or prance
He refused to leave the stable and backed into his stall
He walked very slowly with his head hanging down sadly
He lay down in the middle of the road and would not rise
questions.evidence: it seemed as if I must jump, or dance, or prance

questions.q: What did John say to calm Black Beauty when he was full of spirit?
choices: "Steady, steady, my boy"
"Bad horse! Stop that at once!"
"Go home now, back to your box"
"Whoa there, Ginger, whoa now"

questions.q: Spirited horses that are not exercised enough are called "skittish." What does skittish mean here?
choices: Jumpy and full of nervous energy
Sick and weak from too little food
Lazy and slow from too much rest
Thin and hungry from poor oats
questions.evidence: are often called skittish, when it is only play

questions.q: Why did John not punish Black Beauty for being lively?
choices: He knew it was only high spirits
He was afraid of being thrown off
The squire had told him not to
He was too busy to notice it
questions.evidence: he knew it was only high spirits

questions.q: Why did the horses get their liberty on fine summer Sundays?
choices: The carriage never went out on Sundays because the church was near
Sunday was the one day John spent cleaning out the whole stable
The squire and his family went away to London every Sunday
It was always far too hot for the horses to work on Sundays
questions.evidence: The carriage never went out on Sundays

questions.q: Where did the horses stand to talk on Sundays in the paddock?
choices: Under the shade of the large chestnut tree
Beside the old watermill at the bottom of the field
Inside the coach house out of the hot sun
Next to the gate that led to the church
questions.evidence: under the shade of the large chestnut tree
